Subject: Initial RFI: offline hosting constraints + operator playbook

Connor —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As part of our board-level review we need a concise RFI response that covers running Redwood in an offline / air-gapped environment in our datacenters. High level asks below — we added a few specifics in the attached RFI form.

Can you cover:
- Supported offline installation modes (VPC-only, fully air-gapped, hub-and-spoke)
- Required outbound endpoints and firewall rules for minimal operation and for optional telemetry/updates
- Patching/upgrade window expectations and operator steps for rollback
- Operator runbook for day 0–30 (install, bootstrap, model load, emergency rollback)
- How licensing/entitlements work offline (activation, key rotation)
- Hardware/OS/drivers you’ve validated and minimum resource profiles

We also need a short operator playbook we can share with our SREs (2–3 pages) and any sample network diagrams. Can you get this by EOD Aug 14?

Thanks —
Tim

Subject: Re: Initial RFI: offline hosting constraints + operator playbook

Tim —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is our operator playbook (operator_playbook_v1.pdf) and a concise network diagram (redwood_network_diagram_v2.png). High-level answers below; I called out "mandatory" vs "optional" where it matters.

1) Supported offline installation modes
- Fully air-gapped: supported. Customers receive an installation bundle (signed tarball + checksum) and a one-time entitlement token. This bundle contains the runtime, model artifacts (if requested), and a package manifest for installers.
- VPC-only (no internet egress): supported with optional telemetry proxies.
- Hub-and-spoke (central update service in a DMZ): supported and recommended for fleets.

2) Required outbound endpoints (minimal operation — MANDATORY)
- None for fully air-gapped if you deploy with the pre-bundled artifacts and entitlement token.
- For installations that require updates/metrics (OPTIONAL): outbound to telemetry.redwood.ai:443 and updates.redwood.ai:443. If blocked, use our update-proxy appliance (edge-sync) — instructions in section 3 of the attached playbook.

3) Patching/upgrade windows and rollback
- Typical upgrade requires a rolling restart of inference nodes; for a single-region cluster with N+1 capacity, plan a 2–4 hour maintenance window (including pre-flight checks, binary swap, model warm-up, smoke tests).
- Rollback path: we support immediate rollback to the previously pinned model/runtime within the orchestration UI and via CLI. The operator playbook includes the exact commands and health checks to validate (see "Rollback checklist", page 6).

4) Day 0–30 operator runbook (summary)
- Day 0: Validate image checksum, install runtime on control plane node, register entitlement token, seed model artifacts, smoke test generator and embeddings routes. (Checklist included.)
- Day 7: Confirm KV cache behavior under sampled traffic, enable persistent KV snapshots (optional).
- Day 30: Perform full restore test to an isolated env; confirm audit logging and backup retention.

5) Offline licensing/entitlements
- Activation: one-time signed entitlement file (PKCS7) generated by Redwood, delivered via secure transfer. Activation is performed offline via CLI (entitlement apply --file).
- Rotation: we support key rotation via manual apply; automated rotation requires outbound connectivity.

6) Validated hardware / software matrix (summary)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (primary), RHEL 9 (supported), Rocky Linux 9 (tested).
- GPUs: NVIDIA A10/A100 (driver 520+), systems tested with 1–8 GPUs per node. 2x A100 recommended for production.
- Minimum: 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM, 200GB NVMe for small test cluster.

Operational notes:
- Supply chain & binary verification: all shipped artifacts are signed. Our playbook describes how to verify signatures and checksums (page 2).
- Backup/restore: built-in snapshot/export utilities for KV and checkpointing models. Cold backups stored as tarballs; restore documented in playbook.

Attachments:
- operator_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB) — 8 pages, includes step-by-step commands, health checks, and sample runbook
- redwood_network_diagram_v2.png (image/png, 420KB) — shows DMZ/hub-proxy option and fully air-gapped layout

I'll flag two items that need follow-up before we finalize the deliverable:
- If you want us to include pre-bundled model weights we will need an export request (license & size requirements) — that will add ~3 business days.
- For automated license rotation we require periodic outbound access or a customer-run sync server; if you prefer purely manual rotation we can document that in the playbook.

We can host a 90–120 minute technical workshop for your SREs to walk through the playbook and do a dry run. Proposed slots: week of Aug 21 (US time). Let me know a preferred day and we'll send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer
